title: 018 · Why? #6: a chord slides into the tangent, slope 2 (what a derivative is; predict-first, white)

captions.instagram:
NDA Maths · Derivatives. Slide the two points together on y = x². The line's slope becomes…? A 1 · B 2 · C ∞ 👇

B. The line through (1, 1) and (1 + h, (1 + h)²) has slope ((1 + h)² − 1) ÷ h = 2 + h.
Shrink the gap h and the slope settles on 2: the line becomes the tangent. That limit IS the derivative: f′(1) = 2.
Zoom in far enough and the curve itself looks straight. That's why every smooth curve has a tangent.
Trap: not ∞. 0 ÷ 0 looks scary, but the h cancels before it reaches 0.

NDA asked it in 2021 (II), Q100: the tangent to x² = y at (1, 1) makes angle θ with the x-axis. tan θ = 2, so π/3 < θ < π/2.
